Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

Sorcerer is a one-build class this season and this is the build. All of the damage is Firewall's damage-over-time and almost none of it comes from casting Firewall: the Ring of Fire variant means every *other* spell you cast applies the DoT while you stand inside the ring, which the guide describes as 'a rather peculiar build where you invest everything into Firewall but you almost never cast it'. Charged Bolts fires up to ten bolts per cast and each one applies a stack, while the Berú of the Threefold set auto-casts Meteor, Blizzard and Ball Lightning to refresh the ring and pile on hits - and the real skill of the build is staggering those three elemental procs into a two-second cadence so a Ring of Fire is always under you. The standing is genuinely split and the split is the point: Maxroll's push list rates Firewall S, the only Sorcerer build in S, while Maxroll's own overall endgame list keeps it at A and TierListHQ rates the class A. Maxroll's week-1 article reconciles them exactly - Firewall 'outperforms every other build by at least one order of magnitude' in raw DPS 'but is slow and clunky'. The guide's own cons box says the same in fewer words: very tanky, excellent AoE, good damage, against tricky to play, depends on a set, can't go very fast. The structural weakness is unfixable rather than a gearing problem: 'the moment you leave the Ring of Fire you suddenly deal no damage'. Nothing else the class offers comes close - Hydra, Frozen Orb and Meteor are D tier on both Maxroll lists - so read this as one exceptional build on a mid-tier class, not as a strong class.

Rotation
  1. Open with Unstable Currents and Ice Armor, then stagger the procs onto a two-second cadence - Charged Bolts for Shock, Teleport into a body for the second, Hydra for the Cold proc - so there is a Ring of Fire under you at all times.
  2. The manual Firewall on the bar is the safety net for when you misplay the cadence.
Variants

Leveling — Drop Inferno to hold the pack together, spam Firewall on top of them, let the Fireball Enchantment finish trash. Keep one Conjuration alive for the cooldown reduction and Vulnerable, and Ice Armor up permanently. For the extra teleports from Wormhole, the exact sequence is Teleport, Evade, Teleport, Teleport. Resource note: this variant casts Firewall manually, so you need a resource aspect - Aspect of Elemental Acuity is the best, Prodigy's and Vulpine's are adequate, and Mana Regeneration rolls will do if you have none.
Move on when The guide's own words: 'you can transition to endgame variant of the build when you complete Berú of the Threefold set'. Until then you are casting Firewall yourself; after it, the set casts your other elements for you and the whole build inverts.

Early Endgame — This is the stagger, and it is the build. Open with Unstable Currents and Ice Armor, then shoot Charged Bolts at an enemy - that procs the set and drops a Firewall under you. Keep casting only Charged Bolts for a couple more seconds, then Teleport into an enemy (it has to connect) for a second proc and a second Firewall. Wait another two seconds and cast Hydra for the Cold proc. Now all three procs are cycling every two seconds and there is a Firewall on your screen at all times. The Shock proc fires every six seconds 'like a clockwork and you can't really stop it'; only Frost and Pyromancy are steerable. Manual Firewall on the bar is a safety net for when you misplay the cadence.
Move on when The guide runs identical skill text for Midgame and Endgame, so there is no bar change to wait for - the gate is gearing. Move on once you are filling in the mythic priority list and can start tuning cooldown reduction and masterworking rather than just surviving.

Late Endgame — The same stagger - Unstable Currents and Ice Armor up, Charged Bolts to proc Shock, Teleport into a body for the second proc, Hydra for the Cold proc, then hold the cadence. What changes at this stage is tuning rather than gameplay: enough cooldown reduction to keep Ice Armor and Unstable Currents rolling, and the 15:7 masterwork ratio.
Move on when Only when the content justifies it, and the guide sets the bar in capitals: high-tier Pit or Tower where every run takes at least six to seven minutes. The push variant is a different set with a different gearing rule, not an upgrade.

Pushing — AoE: spam Ice Armor and Unstable Currents on cooldown, keep Firewall permanently active, and divide the rest of your time between Teleport and Blizzard - Teleport to keep the Cauldron set stacked and to group mobs, Blizzard to spend the mana for the Hydra Enchantment and land direct-damage instances. Single target: hold Charged Bolts, Firewall and Unstable Currents off cooldown, Teleport every two to three seconds to hold the stack, and recast Ice Armor when it breaks.

Stat requirements
  • Masterwork to a 15:7 ratio between [100% + total Damage Over Time Multiplier] and [100% + total Vulnerable Multiplier]
Lootfilter

Firewall Sorcerer — Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The guide ships three strictness tiers as import codes in its Loot Filter section, and its changelog records a 2026-07-07 fix to them, so the codes on the page are the corrected ones. Checked and stated honestly: diablo4lootfilter.com carries no Firewall filter at all - its only Sorcerer entries are two Ball Lightning filters and a Season 13 Chain Lightning one, all wrong build and two of them a season stale - so no community permalink is offered here rather than a bad match being dressed up as one.

Uniques
  • helm Target-farm Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint. Mythic priority #3 in the guide's own ordering, worth roughly 15% damage. Where →
  • chest Target-farm Bartuc. Mythic priority #1 - the guide values it at about 43% toughness, and explicitly rejects Tyrael's Might as a replacement because it is 'quite a bit worse defensively than Raiment of the Infinite and the damage gain is not very noticeable'. Where →
  • ring 2 Target-farm Andariel. Mythic priority #2, worth roughly 21% damage. Where →
  • pants Push variant only. No dedicated boss this season - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so farm it via the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. The guide offers Aspect of Disobedience pants as the alternative if Tibault's Will leaves you too squishy, in which case swap one jewelry temper to Lucky Hit: Chance to Restore Resource. Where →

Skill point priority

  1. Scope note: the guide publishes no levelling build - 'this build guide assumes you have a Level 70 Character and unlocked Torment 1' - so this stage records its Starter variant, which is the earliest setup it does publish. The intro does say Firewall 'is a very good early game spell that can be used to level to 70', so the skills are right even though the route is not published

  4. Ice Armor is the main defensive skill - keep it active as much as possible
  5. Teleport for mobility; Wormhole is what makes the extra-teleport sequence work
  6. Hydra and Familiar as Conjurations: both reduce cooldowns and make enemies Vulnerable via Aspect of Shredding Blades. One out at a time is enough - Hydra against single targets or when you need the healing, Familiar for AoE

Skill point priority

  1. Charged Bolts becomes the main attack: up to ten bolts per cast, each applying a stack of Firewall's DoT while you stand in the ring. Use it in melee range so every bolt connects
  2. Firewall is demoted to 'a supplementary skill that you only rarely cast when you run out of Rings'
  3. Unstable Currents - a long-cooldown buff that adds extra hits to every spell, meaning more Firewall DoTs
  4. Ice Armor kept active as much as possible
  5. Teleport, but proc your set or Enchantment first or it goes on cooldown for nothing
  6. Off-bar investment is mandatory here and easy to miss: points go into Lightning Spear and Chain Lightning (cast by Unstable Currents) and into Meteor, Blizzard and Ball Lightning (cast by Berú of the Threefold), purely for the extra hits and the Overpower and Ferocity they generate

Skill point priority

  1. Charged Bolts, Firewall, Unstable Currents, Ice Armor and Teleport as before - the bar does not change from the early endgame
  2. Keep the off-bar points in Lightning Spear, Chain Lightning, Meteor, Blizzard and Ball Lightning: they are cast for you and every hit is a DoT stack
  3. Cooldown reduction becomes a real stat here: 'this build likes to have a bit more CDR than usual so you usually want 1-2 extra rolls besides you hat and tempers on Jewelry', to hold Ice Armor and Unstable Currents and to keep manual Firewall available when the set is on cooldown
  4. Masterworking has an explicit target ratio: spread crits on weapon, gloves and jewelry between Damage Over Time and Vulnerable multipliers so that [100% + total DoT multi] to [100% + total Vulnerable multi] sits at 15:7
  5. Speedfarming sub-variant, if you want it: pull points out of Hydra into Fire Bolt, which becomes the spam skill - fewer hits than Charged Bolts but constant Overpower, so you Teleport far more often

Skill point priority

  1. Read the guide's warning first, in its own capitals: this variant is only good for pushing, meaning high-tier Pit or Tower where every run takes at least six to seven minutes, and 'it's terrible for literally anything else you can do in the game'

  6. The inversion to understand: this set swaps Berú of the Threefold for Berú of the Cauldron, which makes cooldown reduction actively bad - Ancient Flame turns cooldown reduction directly into lost Firewall damage, so cap out at four to five rolls including tempers

Plan

Stated plainly, because the honest answer is unusual here: this guide publishes War Plans *widgets* but no War Plans prose. The only text under the section, repeated identically for all five variants, is 'selected nodes are what I consider mandatory, the rest is up to personal preference'. The picks below are therefore decoded from the guide's own planner payload rather than quoted from the article, and the payload allocates five of the seven activity trees - it touches Nightmare Dungeons, Helltide, Kurast Undercity, Lair Bosses and The Pit, and leaves Tree of Whispers and Infernal Hordes empty. That is the author's own board, so it is real build-specific data; it simply arrives without an explanation, and no explanation has been invented for it.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

Sorcerer is a one-build class this season and this is the build. All of the damage is Firewall's damage-over-time and almost none of it comes from casting Firewall: the Ring of Fire variant means every *other* spell you cast applies the DoT while you stand inside the ring, which the guide describes as 'a rather peculiar build where you invest everything into Firewall but you almost never cast it'. Charged Bolts fires up to ten bolts per cast and each one applies a stack, while the Berú of the Threefold set auto-casts Meteor, Blizzard and Ball Lightning to refresh the ring and pile on hits - and the real skill of the build is staggering those three elemental procs into a two-second cadence so a Ring of Fire is always under you. The standing is genuinely split and the split is the point: Maxroll's push list rates Firewall S, the only Sorcerer build in S, while Maxroll's own overall endgame list keeps it at A and TierListHQ rates the class A. Maxroll's week-1 article reconciles them exactly - Firewall 'outperforms every other build by at least one order of magnitude' in raw DPS 'but is slow and clunky'. The guide's own cons box says the same in fewer words: very tanky, excellent AoE, good damage, against tricky to play, depends on a set, can't go very fast. The structural weakness is unfixable rather than a gearing problem: 'the moment you leave the Ring of Fire you suddenly deal no damage'. Nothing else the class offers comes close - Hydra, Frozen Orb and Meteor are D tier on both Maxroll lists - so read this as one exceptional build on a mid-tier class, not as a strong class.

Rotation
  1. Open with Unstable Currents and Ice Armor, then stagger the procs onto a two-second cadence - Charged Bolts for Shock, Teleport into a body for the second, Hydra for the Cold proc - so there is a Ring of Fire under you at all times.
  2. The manual Firewall on the bar is the safety net for when you misplay the cadence.
Variants

Leveling — Drop Inferno to hold the pack together, spam Firewall on top of them, let the Fireball Enchantment finish trash. Keep one Conjuration alive for the cooldown reduction and Vulnerable, and Ice Armor up permanently. For the extra teleports from Wormhole, the exact sequence is Teleport, Evade, Teleport, Teleport. Resource note: this variant casts Firewall manually, so you need a resource aspect - Aspect of Elemental Acuity is the best, Prodigy's and Vulpine's are adequate, and Mana Regeneration rolls will do if you have none.
Move on when The guide's own words: 'you can transition to endgame variant of the build when you complete Berú of the Threefold set'. Until then you are casting Firewall yourself; after it, the set casts your other elements for you and the whole build inverts.

Early Endgame — This is the stagger, and it is the build. Open with Unstable Currents and Ice Armor, then shoot Charged Bolts at an enemy - that procs the set and drops a Firewall under you. Keep casting only Charged Bolts for a couple more seconds, then Teleport into an enemy (it has to connect) for a second proc and a second Firewall. Wait another two seconds and cast Hydra for the Cold proc. Now all three procs are cycling every two seconds and there is a Firewall on your screen at all times. The Shock proc fires every six seconds 'like a clockwork and you can't really stop it'; only Frost and Pyromancy are steerable. Manual Firewall on the bar is a safety net for when you misplay the cadence.
Move on when The guide runs identical skill text for Midgame and Endgame, so there is no bar change to wait for - the gate is gearing. Move on once you are filling in the mythic priority list and can start tuning cooldown reduction and masterworking rather than just surviving.

Late Endgame — The same stagger - Unstable Currents and Ice Armor up, Charged Bolts to proc Shock, Teleport into a body for the second proc, Hydra for the Cold proc, then hold the cadence. What changes at this stage is tuning rather than gameplay: enough cooldown reduction to keep Ice Armor and Unstable Currents rolling, and the 15:7 masterwork ratio.
Move on when Only when the content justifies it, and the guide sets the bar in capitals: high-tier Pit or Tower where every run takes at least six to seven minutes. The push variant is a different set with a different gearing rule, not an upgrade.

Pushing — AoE: spam Ice Armor and Unstable Currents on cooldown, keep Firewall permanently active, and divide the rest of your time between Teleport and Blizzard - Teleport to keep the Cauldron set stacked and to group mobs, Blizzard to spend the mana for the Hydra Enchantment and land direct-damage instances. Single target: hold Charged Bolts, Firewall and Unstable Currents off cooldown, Teleport every two to three seconds to hold the stack, and recast Ice Armor when it breaks.

Stat requirements
  • Masterwork to a 15:7 ratio between [100% + total Damage Over Time Multiplier] and [100% + total Vulnerable Multiplier]

Hydra

ConjurationFire

Rank 1/15

Mana Cost: 20

Lucky Hit Chance: 5.0%

Summon a 3-headed Hydra for 10.0 seconds. Each head spits fire at enemies, dealing 35% damage.

You may have up to 1 Hydra active at a time.

Modifiers

  • Cooldown ReductionHydra reduces the Cooldown of a random Skill by 0.3 seconds whenever it attacks.
  • HealingHydra heals you for 1% of your Maximum Life ({x}) each time it deals damage.
  • Frigid HydraHydra becomes a Frost Skill that deals 43.75% Cold damage. Hydra's attacks pierce enemies and Chill for 15%.

MasteryFire

Rank 15/15

Mana Cost: 40

Lucky Hit Chance: 30%

Create a wall of fire, dealing 300% Burning damage over 3.5 seconds. Enemies continue Burning for 1.8 seconds after leaving the wall.

Modifiers

  • WildfireFirewall's Size is increased by 50% and duration increased to 7.0 seconds.
  • Cost ReductionEvery 100 Mana spent makes your next Firewall cost no Mana, stacking up to 300 total Mana.
  • Damage BonusFirewall deals 75%[x] increased damage, but its duration is reduced by 25%[+].

Thrillseeker

PassiveSubo

Your active Cooldowns are reduced by 0.5 seconds when an Explosive Charge explodes.

Explosive Charges now detonate after only 1.5 seconds.

Bargaining Chips

PassiveSubo

Targets stuck with Explosive Charges take 5%[x] increased damage per Explosive Charge stuck.

Incendiary Bolt

PassiveSubo

If Subo's Snipe hits the target he originally aimed at, a Molotov explodes on them.

Ambusher

PassiveSubo

You gain 20%[x] Lucky Hit Chance against enemies damaged by Subo's Salvo within the last 3 seconds.

Share a Drink

PassiveSubo

When one of Subo's Molotovs explodes, it has a 50% chance to drop a Healing Potion for you.

Scorched Earth

PassiveSubo

Subo's initial Molotov explosions cause enemies to take 30%[x] increased Damage Over Time from you for 3 seconds.

Mastermind

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Trap and Trip Mines explosions gain 60% Size.

You and Subo gain 25%[+] Crowd Control Duration.

Loaded Munitions

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Traps and Trip Mines inflict Vulnerable on enemies for 5 seconds.

Opening Fire

PassiveSubo

You deal 25%[x] increased Critical Strike Damage to enemies hit by Subo's Cover Fire for 4 seconds.

Pin Cushion

PassiveSubo

Subo's Cover Fire also Immobilizes enemies for 3 seconds.

Ready At Hand

PassiveSubo

Direct damage to an Elite grants you 20%[+] Movement Speed for 2 seconds.

Piercing Arrows

PassiveSubo

Subo's Heavy Shot now pierces through enemies.

Trip Mines

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 18 seconds

Subo scatters 3 explosive traps that each arm after 1.0 seconds. When an enemy moves within range of one, it explodes for 300% Physical damage and Knocks Down enemies for 1.5 seconds.

Cover Fire

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a countless volley of arrows, then unleashes it over your position for 140% Physical damage that Slows enemies by 50% for 4 seconds.

Explosive Charge

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Subo fires 4 Explosive Charges that stick to enemies. Each explodes after 6.5 seconds or when their target dies, dealing 60% Physical damage.

Snipe

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a massive piercing bolt, then unleashes it forwards for 450% Physical damage that Knocks Back enemies.

Wire Trap

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 10 seconds

Weapon: Bow

Basic Attack: Heavy Shot

Subo places a concussive trap that arms after 0.8 seconds. When an enemy moves within range, it explodes for 80% Physical damage and Stuns enemies for 2.0 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo fires a toughened arrow at an enemy, dealing 80% Physical damage with a 30% chance to Stun for 1.0 seconds.

Molotov

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Crossbow

Basic Attack: Salvo

Subo tosses an incendiary at an enemy, dealing 10% Physical damage and Stunning them for 1.0 seconds before exploding into flames. For the next 5 seconds, enemies within the area repeatedly take 36% Burning damage over 3 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo launches 5 bolts at an enemy, each dealing 30% Physical damage. The final bolt explodes, Slowing enemies by 50% for 2 seconds.

Tree of Plenty

Tree of Whispers

The Tree offers a fourth Whisper Cache choice.

Headrotten Feast

Tree of Whispers

Headrotten Bosses that are drawn to Exposed Roots have +1 Monster Power, and will always drop a Whisper Cache.

Resplendent Favor

Tree of Whispers

Each Whisper Cache has a chance to drop a Resplendent Spark.

Malignant Invasion

Tree of Whispers

Varshan can now appear in a Whisper Ambushes.

Slay Varshan to earn the contents of an Ancestral Collection of Chaos .

Grim Retribution

Tree of Whispers

Completing a Whisper has a chance to trigger a Whisper Ambush.

These enemies have a chance to burst out the contents of a Collection of Chaos when slain.

Roots of Power

Tree of Whispers

Enemies that are drawn to Exposed Roots have +1 Monster Power.

Planting Corrupted Roots in Helltides yields double rewards.

Colossal Foe

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Ambushes sometimes include Bosses.

These Bosses will always burst out the contents of a Greater Collection of Chaos when slain.

Simple Gifts

Tree of Whispers

The Tree only offers one Whisper Cache choice that will always be a Material Collection or a Collection of Chaos.

Corrupted Roots

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Caches sometimes contain Corrupted Roots.

Plant Corrupted Roots to grow an Exposed Root. These will attract nearby enemies, and have a chance to grow larger and summon more fearsome enemies.

The regions of Sanctuary each bear different fruit.

Wisdom of Whispers

Tree of Whispers

Gain 50% more Experience Orbs in Whisper Caches.

Fortune or Famine

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Caches from the Tree of Whispers are always at least of Greater Quality... or Junk.

Material Wealth

Tree of Whispers

The Tree now only offers Material Collections.

Grim Mysteries

Tree of Whispers

Collections of Chaos are replaced with Collections of Mysteries.

These caches can drop anything.

Chaotic Favor

Tree of Whispers

Completing a Whisper has a small chance to award a Collection of Chaos.

Branching Pathways

Nightmare Dungeons

When advancing to the next dungeon in a Nightmare Escalation, 2 additional Horadric Portals appear.

Fearless Conviction

Nightmare Dungeons

While in a Nightmare Dungeon, killing Elites and Champions grants you stacks of Conviction.

Getting hit by an Elite or Champion causes you to lose a stack of Conviction.

A Conviction Chest appears at the end of the dungeon that grants rewards for each remaining Conviction. This chest has a higher than normal chance to award Attuned Primordial Dust.

Goblinfall

Nightmare Dungeons

Treasure Goblins have a small chance to drop a Nightmare Sigil with the Treasure Breach affix.

Nemesis

Nightmare Dungeons

Activating a Shrine in a Nightmare Dungeon causes up to 7 Elites to ambush you.

Gauntlet

Nightmare Dungeons

While in a Nightmare Dungeon, slaying an enemy while empowered by a Shrine traps their soul within you.

When the Shrine buff expires, all trapped souls escape and spawn around you as renewed enemies.

Souls will be lost when moving between dungeons in an Escalation Dungeon.

Horadric Hunter

Nightmare Dungeons

Kill 25 Elites across Nightmare Dungeons to reveal a Horadric Altar. Activating it results in one of the following outcomes:

Summon Elites

Summon Treasure Goblins

Summon The Butcher

Gain Riches

Terrible Misfortune

Altar of Avarice

Nightmare Dungeons

Horadric Altars are replaced with Goblin Altars that only summon Treasure Goblins.

Cipher Maps

Nightmare Dungeons

Whenever you would reveal a Horadric Altar, you reveal 2 instead.

Rewarded Faith

Nightmare Dungeons

Gain a random additional buff when claiming a Shrine in a Nightmare Dungeon.

Greed is Good

Nightmare Dungeons

Killing a Treasure Goblin in a Nightmare Dungeon has a small chance to spawn a portal that takes you to the Goblin's Retreat.

Waking Spoils

Nightmare Dungeons

After completing a Nightmare Dungeon, a War's Bounty Chest will spawn that grants additional rewards.

Recurring Nightmare

Nightmare Dungeons

Bosses in Nightmare Dungeons gain +1 Monster Power and have a chance to drop an Escalation Sigil when slain.

Escalation Sigils can only appear in Torment+ difficulty.

Dread Revival

Nightmare Dungeons

Bosses in Nightmare Dungeons have a chance to revive when slain.

Night Terrors

Helltide

You have a chance to be ambushed by Hellborne in Nightmare Dungeons.

Hellborne have a small chance to drop a Profane Mindcage when slain.

Hell's Prize

Helltide

Hell's Prize chests will now appear in Helltide.

These chests offer a massive torrent of items for 666 Aberrant Cinders.

Fall of the Fell

Helltide

Harbingers will emerge from falling meteors twice as often, and drop twice as many Aberrant Cinders when slain.

Harbingers in Helltide have +1 Monster Power.

Meat Brothers

Helltide

Instead of Hellborne, two Butchers that are connected with flaming chains ambush you.

These Butchers each have a high chance to drop a Profane Mindcage when slain.

Hellmouth

Helltide

When a Hellwyrm emerges, it unleashes one of the following:

A Chaos Rift, which releases varied rewards upon collapse.

Maggots, which burst out Experience Orbs when slain.

Bloodseekers, which are more likely to drop Ancestral items when slain.

Wretched Vermin

Helltide

Demonic Rats will frequently attack you in Helltide.

Ashes to Ashes

Helltide

On death, lose all your Aberrant Cinders.

For every 100 Aberrant Cinders you pick up, you gain an additional 10.

Undying Embers

Helltide

You lose no Aberrant Cinders on death.

Infernal Rite

Helltide

Ambushes spawn up to four additional Hellborne.

Hellborne have a higher chance to drop Unique items when slain.

Planar Tremors

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always open a Chaos Rift, and enemies that emerge from it gain +1 Monster Power.

The first time a Chaos Rift opens, there is a chance that another will open.

Tainted Shrines

Helltide

While empowered by a Shrine in Helltide, slain enemies grant double the progress to your Threat Level.

Hated Foe

Helltide

Maximum Threat enemies that ambush you gain +1 Monster Power.

Chaotic Echoes

Helltide

Collapsed Chaos Rifts have a chance to reopen.

Bursting Brood

Helltide

Maggots and Pangs of Duriel explode when killed and will often drop Boss Trophies.

Writhe and Rot

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always spew Maggots that gain +1 Monster Power.

Sometimes, a Pang of Duriel will also crawl forth. Lair Keys often burst out of Pangs of Duriel.

Bound by Blood

Helltide

Bloodseekers are connected with flaming chains.

When slain, Bloodseekers drop items that match the category of the last opened Tortured Gift.

Crimson Scent

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always call forth Bloodseekers that gain +1 Monster Power.

Greater Bloodseekers may also emerge, which have a high chance to drop Legendary items when slain.

Idols of War

The Undercity

Greater Tributes of Armament more frequently drop throughout Sanctuary and have an additional Bargain choices.

Trials and Tributes

The Undercity

For each Portal Prankster you slay within the Undercity, a Tribute Chest appears after killing the District Boss.

Tribute Chests are unlocked by offering a Tribute.

Gutter Filth

The Undercity

When you activate any Beacon within the Undercity, there is a small chance to summon a Portal Prankster.

Invasion Portals will sometimes summon Rats of varying amounts.

Endless Swarm

The Undercity

Invasion Portals now appear in the Undercity.

The enemies that emerge grant Attunement when slain.

Jade Epiphany

The Undercity

When you gain an Attunement level in the Undercity, Experience Orbs appear around you.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Finely Tuned

The Undercity

Gain additional Tuning Prisms when completing the Undercity at maximum Attunement.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Pathfinder

The Undercity

When you reach maximum Attunement, a portal to the final floor of the Undercity appears.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Unfortunate Souls

The Undercity

Invasion Portals can now summon Wisps that attach to you and vanish if you die.

Each Wisp you save will reward you with Forgotten Souls and other Crafting Materials at the end of the run.

Initiative

The Undercity

When you find the District Boss you gain the Initiative buff, which has a duration equal to your remaining Time. Initiative is lost upon death.

If you slay the District Boss with Initiative active, you receive Tribute rewards as if your Attunement was 2 higher (max 6).

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Last Gasp

The Undercity

Time collected from slain enemies with 5 seconds or less remaining in the Undercity doubles the Time earned.

Bauble Day

The Undercity

If you slay a Portal Prankster within the Undercity, the Cabochon Merchant will appear after killing the District Boss.

The Cabochon Merchant will sell you Runes and Gems for Gold.

Lair Bosses

Gain +1 Hoard Chest when you slay a Lair Boss (excluding Belial).

Infernal Deception

Lair Bosses

Belial can now ambush you after completing the Infernal Hordes.

Two by Two

Lair Bosses

After opening a Hoard Chest, there is a low chance a Portal will open that will take you to the Nemesis Lair, where you will fight two Initiate Lair Bosses at the same time.

Slaying both will yield great rewards.

You cannot enter a Nemesis Lair from Belial's throne room.

Nemesis Tides

Lair Bosses

Killing Lair Bosses in Helltides while earning the Event Mastery grants many random Lair Boss materials.

This only occurs in Torment+ difficulties.

Lair Bosses

Hoard Chests drop one additional Unique Item, but it can be for any Class.

Greater Nemesis

Lair Bosses

After completing a Nemesis Lair, there is a chance that a portal will appear that will take you to a Greater Nemesis Lair. Within this heinous place lies two Greater Lair Bosses.

Slaying both bosses will yield great rewards.

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses have a higher chances of dropping specific Runes.

Lair Bosses

After defeating all Bosses within the Greater Nemesis Lair, the Call Of Evil will appear. This altar will accept 3 Superior Lair Keys and open a Portal that takes you to the Ultimate Nemesis Lair.

Inside the Ultimate Nemesis Lair, all enemies gain +5 Monster Power. Defeating the Boss Encounter will award you with 10 Hoard Chests worth of Items.

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses

Bartuc and the Fell Council have +1 Monster Power and drop additional items when slain.

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hoard

Infernal Hordes

Defeating either the Fell Council or Bartuc reveals the Hoard of Greater Equipment, which contains a colossal deluge of equipment and other rewards.

Forged in Flame

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Your Infernal Offerings are more likely to share a category with your previous choice.

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Infernal Hordes

Choron's Haste

The Pit

The Pit gains the Haste Mastery objective.

When you kill the Guardian gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for every 5 minutes left on the Timer.

Damned Thieves

The Pit

Orb Thieves have a chance to spawn in The Pit.

Orb Thieves drop an immense amount of Progress Orbs when killed, but leave a trail of Traps in their wake.

Heart of Stone

The Pit

Begin The Pit carrying the Heart of Stone, a fragile relic that is dropped after taking sustained damage and breaks after dropping 10 times.

While you carry it, enemies can drop bonus Progress Orbs.

After slaying the Guardian, Choron's Pedestal appears. Deposit the Heart of Stone within to gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance.

Choron's Blessing

The Pit

Gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for completing The Pit.

Choron's Favor

The Pit

Special events and encounters become more common in higher Difficulty Tiers of The Pit.

Choron's Soul

The Pit

Choron's Soul now spawns with the Awakened Glyphstone.

Choron's Soul will drop 1 Progress Orb per Glyph Upgrade Chance offered.

All Progress Orbs in The Pit now grant Experience.

Choron's Flesh

The Pit

Choron's Flesh now spawns with the Awakened Glyphstone.

Choron's Flesh will allow you to get valuable Equipment by consuming one of your Glyph Upgrade Chances.

Choron's Shortcut

The Pit

Choron's Portal randomly appears in The Pit.

When used, it will send you to the entrance to the next Pit Floor, or become Unstable and summon either an Elite or a Shrine.

Cursed Rituals

The Pit

Different Ritual Sites now spawn in the Pit, and special Materials can spawn in different environments:

Choron's Blood appears in foliage dense regions

Choron's Sweat appears in stony locations

Choron's Tears appears in mystical places

Sacrificing these Materials at Ritual Sites may grant Gold, Materials, Items, and more.

The Pit

The Butcher has a chance to appear anywhere in The Pit.

The Butcher is a Guardian and killing him will complete the run.

However, you fail the run if he kills any player.

Cursed Merchant

The Pit

The Cursed Merchant has a chance to appear when completing the Pit.

The Cursed Merchant will sell Equipment for Artificers Stones.

Cursed Offerings

The Pit

Cursed Machines have a chance to appear while exploring the Pit.

Cursed Machines cost Artificers Stones to activate. Activating one will grant you valuable materials and attract vicious enemies.

The more Cursed Machines you find in a single Pit run, the more lucrative the rewards will become.

Choron's Wager

The Pit

Choron's Wager can appear in The Pit.
